real_estate.homebuilder: Rates jumped to 7.30% after October's inflation report came in hotter than forecast.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average jumped to 7.30% Tuesday, up 0.12, and the 15-year to 6.92%, up 0.09, after October's consumer prices rose faster than forecast. Wednesday is Veterans Day and the bond market is closed, so no new reading is posted yet. At 7.30%, a Fremont buyer at today's $1,299,444 median with 20% down would pay about $7,127 a month in principal and interest, $85 more than at Monday's 7.18%.

Owners are borrowing against their homes at a pace not seen in two decades. Home equity line balances rose $23 billion in the third quarter to $481 billion, the largest increase since 2005, the New York Fed reported Tuesday, while mortgage balances rose $257 billion to $13.4 trillion.

The board wide table is 2,399, from 2,419 Tuesday, with 150 coming soon and 144 brand new. The five city ledger is 628, from 623: Hayward (180) added four, Fremont (217) three and Milpitas (95) one, while Newark (76) fell two and Union City (60) one.

What this means for you: a 0.12 jump adds about $85 a month on the median Fremont home, so if you are ready to lock, talk with your lender about locking now or floating. On Veterans Day, a note for those who served: Mortgage News Daily's 30-year VA average is 6.90%, 0.40 below the conventional rate. Sellers, 190 homes in our five cities have been listed 60 days or longer.

• Board wide: 2,399 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 150 coming soon and 144 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 628 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 556 are on the market and 72 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 217 live, 172 active, 33 coming soon, 11 brand new and 1 back on the market. The median on market list price is $1,299,444 at $790 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 36 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 180, Milpitas 95, Newark 76, Union City 60.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,038,444 at $666 a square foot. 273 homes are priced under a million, and 190 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.note: Levels are Tuesday, November 10 at the closing bell. Live at 10:59 AM PT Wednesday: Dow up 0.50%, S&P 500 up 1.63%, Nasdaq up 2.22%.
stocks.news:
Chip stocks are roaring back. As of 10:59 AM PT the Philadelphia semiconductor index is up 7.3%, the Nasdaq 2.22%, the S&P 500 1.63% and the Dow 0.50%, after TSMC reported record October sales and CoreWeave, which rents out AI computing power, raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $13.0 billion to $13.3 billion. CoreWeave is up 25.8% and Fremont's Lam Research 8.2%. Tuesday went the other way after the inflation report: the S&P 500 fell 0.38%, the Nasdaq 0.74% and the Dow 0.30%.

Anthropic, the San Francisco AI company, set the terms of its initial public offering Tuesday: 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, or $57.8 billion to $64.4 billion, to trade on Nasdaq as ANT, according to its SEC filing (chart). Even the low end would make it the second largest IPO ever, behind SpaceX's $75.0 billion in June. Up to 20% of the shares are expected to go to individual investors, through brokers including Schwab, Fidelity and Robinhood. A deal that size creates a lot of paper wealth within a BART ride of Fremont, though insiders are locked up for months after the listing.

TSMC's October revenue was NT$586.89 billion, up 59.7% from a year earlier and 14.7% from September, its biggest month on record (chart). TSMC builds the chips that Bay Area companies such as Nvidia and Apple design, so its sales are a read on AI demand here.

economy.note: Levels are Tuesday, November 10: the 10-Year is Treasury's close, gold and silver are COMEX December settlements, and Brent is the ICE January settlement. Live at 10:59 AM PT Wednesday: gold $3,996.00 (-0.85%), silver $51.92 (+1.36%), Brent $93.04 (+1.69%); the bond market is closed for Veterans Day.
economy.commentary:
Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% that economists polled by Dow Jones expected, and core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3% against a forecast of 0.2%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Tuesday. Gasoline rose 1.0% and groceries 0.4%. There is no annual rate this month because of the 2025 government shutdown.

Treasury has the 10-Year closing Tuesday at 4.98%, up 0.10, and Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a quarter point rate increase would be appropriate in December. Household debt rose $334 billion in the third quarter to $19.1 trillion, the New York Fed said, with credit card balances up $22 billion to $1.29 trillion.

Gold settled Tuesday at $4,030.20, down 2.05%, silver at $51.23, down 2.79%, and Brent at $91.49, down 1.17%. Two corrections: Market Briefs printed gold at $4,055 (+0.62%) and Brent at $92.41 (+1.01%), overnight prices measured against Tuesday's settlements, and the 10-Year at 5.00%; Treasury has it at 4.98%.
